output.brief:
The August dip was mainly caused by the east chiller (CH-2) failing from 4 to 19 August. It serves floors 6-8. Floors 6-8 room comfort fell from 8.4 to 6.1 and overall from 8.6 to 7.4. Scores on those floors recovered to 8.4 once cooling was restored. 56 of the 74 negative comments were about heat, all from floors 6-8. Floors 1-5 were essentially flat. Cleanliness scores, inspection pass rates and check-in scores did not move. Queue times were stable, and the survey method was unchanged. So the evidence doesn't support blaming Orrin or the kiosks, and I would not serve notice or pull the kiosks. The deferred preventive maintenance on both chillers (April budget hold) and the lack of a spare part on site are the likely root conditions. I'm fairly confident, though I did not collect further evidence, such as the chief engineer interview or the finance memo, to confirm them.

Next steps:
1. Restore the deferred chiller maintenance and keep critical spares on site.
2. Write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages.
3. Don't exclude the August data from the reported score.
4. Keep watching value-for-money on floors 1-5. The 6% rate rise may have added to the usual August dip, but the evidence can't separate the two. Don't reverse the rate rise yet.
